name: Young Canada Works student jobs in heritage
summary: Federally funded summer and student jobs at museums, archives, libraries and heritage sites for students aged 16–30. You apply to employers through the Young Canada Works portal.
whatYouDo: Depending on the employer, you might guide tours, help with collections and archives, run programs and events, or support an organization's outreach. Positions generally last 6 to 16 weeks at 30–40 hours a week. A separate internship stream, Building Careers in Heritage, serves college and university graduates.
appeal: Paid work experience in the arts, culture and heritage sector, which can be hard to break into
Employers set pay. One museum's 2026 postings, funded through YCW or Canada Summer Jobs, paid $18.25/hour for 30 hours a week
Students have no application deadline and apply through one national portal
A graduate stream offers longer internships after college or university
watchOuts: Only for Canadian citizens, permanent residents or people with refugee status. International students and temporary-visa holders are excluded
You must be 16–30 and enrolled in high school, college, CEGEP or university (heritage student stream)
Short-term: usually 6–16 weeks, mainly in summer
Employers do the hiring. The program doesn't place you
The Canadian Museums Association warned a House of Commons committee of a funding cliff that could eliminate 600+ youth jobs, so there may be fewer positions
On-site work at the heritage organization

credentials: Current enrolment in high school, college, CEGEP or university (student stream)

training.notes: No program-level training requirement found; employers train students on the job.

compensation.notes: Wages are set by employers ('competitive for the region', per the Canadian Museums Association). Example: one heritage employer's 2026 postings funded through YCW or Canada Summer Jobs paid $18.25/hour for 30 h/week. Not a program-wide rate.

reliability.notes: Fixed-term placements of 6–16 consecutive weeks at 30–40 h/week (CMA). How many positions exist each year depends on federal funding, which the CMA warned is at risk.

applicationSteps: Create an account on the Young Canada Works portal
Use 'Search for a job' in your account to find heritage positions
Apply to employers through the portal; the employer interviews and hires
Apply early: there's no student deadline, but the government recommends applying before summer
fitsIf: You're a student aged 16–30 (citizen, PR or refugee status) interested in museums, archives, arts or history who wants paid summer experience.
notFitIf: You're not a student, are over 30, hold a temporary visa, or need year-round or remote work.
